mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an easing monetary policy that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the past 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 3.5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 3.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising federal funds rate and falling unemployment rate signals an overheating economy that triggers Fed policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is rising and UNRATE is falling, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a tight labor market (UNRATE < 4.0%), rising wage pressures and potential Fed tightening lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls over the past 3 months signals strong labor market conditions that support corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS has increased over the past 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts exceed 1,500,000 units per month, it signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 1500.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising housing starts and rising industrial production signals robust economic growth that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST and INDPRO are both rising, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In the early-cycle expansion phase, characterized by strong consumer spending (RSAFS > 755,000 million dollars), the S&P 500 tends to outperform due to improving corporate earnings, producing positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS > 755000, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
